record.paper_title: Open Problems in Communication and Computation
record.original_question: Is there a duality between computation and communication?

evidence.quote: Is there a duality between computation and communication?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Within the framework of information theory and theoretical computer science, communication is typically modeled by an encoder–channel–decoder system, in which a source message is mapped into a codeword, transmitted through a noisy channel, and decoded so as to recover the source with low error probability; the fundamental limits are characterized by Shannon's channel coding theorem and rate-distortion theory. Computation, on the other hand, is typically modeled by a Boolean circuit, Turing machine, or algorithm that maps inputs to outputs, with fundamental limits described in terms of time, space, or circuit-size complexity.

Formulate and establish (or refute) a precise duality principle between computation and communication. That is, exhibit an explicit correspondence under which: (i) every communication problem (a triple consisting of a source distribution, a channel, and a fidelity criterion) is associated with a dual computation problem (a function class, model of computation, and a resource measure), and conversely; (ii) optimal achievable rates / capacity-type quantities on the communication side correspond to optimal resource bounds (e.g. circuit size, depth, time, space) on the computation side, in a way that converts direct (achievability) theorems on one side into converse (lower bound) theorems on the other, and vice versa; and (iii) the correspondence is functorial in the sense that composition of channels corresponds to composition of computational reductions.

Either construct such a duality and prove the corresponding equivalence of fundamental limits, or prove that no such duality can exist by exhibiting an obstruction.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as a broad conceptual open problem about a hypothetical duality between computation and communication. While there are partial analogies (e.g. between source/channel coding and circuit/communication complexity, or via interactive coding and information complexity), no general established duality theorem is known to formalize the correspondence, and no definitive negative result rules it out. The status appears open.
